correctness.rationale: Exact gcd and 2-adic reductions give k and the parity dichotomy. Both conjugate roots on the odd-y conic are odd integral and strictly descend except at (1,1), forcing k=4. The odd-coordinate Pell parameterization follows from units of norm minus one in Z[sqrt2]. The even-coordinate complete-square substitution is two-way; mod 4 and 8 prove the converse parity and positivity. For each p=7 mod8, two k residues force a negative-Pell obstruction, and CRT/Mertens give O(X/sqrt(loglog X)), with an additive modulus at most sqrt X. The current embedded script check.py was executed and printed VERIFY_OK; the proof is not inferred from the finite check.

value.rationale: The asymmetric leading coefficient 2 is the first natural anisotropic specialization outside global integral Vieta-jump conditions, and creates a genuine parity transition: the odd chamber collapses to a single Pell orbit parameter while the even chamber admits a different discriminant for each odd parameter. Exact class coverage, the isolated k=3 case, and a global density-zero spectrum give structural information about a natural divisibility family. This is more than renaming a Pell equation or reporting finite calculations.
